reviewed_items.reviewer_notes: All 3 gates passed. Gate 1 skipped: this is a missing-validation finding (absent UNIQUE constraint, not an unreachable function); additionally, the attack bypasses application code entirely via direct Supabase client call permitted by RLS policy (`0000_create_member_schema.sql:83`). Gate 2: BUG_BOUNTY_SCOPE.json contains no `trust_assumptions` table — no lookup possible. Gate 3: `supabase/migrations/` and `src/lib/services/` are both explicitly in-scope. An attacker can trigger this via the Supabase anon-key client (authenticated session) by issuing a self-UPDATE on `member.members.display_name` to match a victim's name — permitted by the unrestricted RLS policy and unconstrained by any UNIQUE index — causing the kiosk screen to display the victim's name to physical observers when the attacker scans their NFC card. Severity held at Medium: impact is kiosk-display impersonation (social/reputational) with no direct data exfiltration or account takeover; no client_diversity cap applies (no deployment_context in scope file).
